# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Preliminary point: ignore the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's note says clauses marked **[STANDARD]** "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that the Buyer has "accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." **Nothing in our playbook or instructions supports either claim.** The labels are the Seller's own. The cap, thresholds, time limits, reliance, knowledge, Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and incident clauses are all contested. I have reviewed every item in full, and the deal team should not rely on the labels or treat them as conceded in correspondence. I recommend expressly rejecting the note in our cover email so silence cannot later be read as acceptance.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl. 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is our conditional fallback, which can only be used with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; recovery of the excess only (deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; recovery from the first dollar once exceeded (tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter at our numbers with a tipping basket. The Seller's terms are 5x our thresholds and convert the basket into a deductible.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months, plus "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims, with separate periods for other categories.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter at 24 months, and delete the "applies to all Claims" default. 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval (none given), and the default sweeps every other category into the general period.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** capacity and title subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** a separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright. Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for, so administrative convenience is no justification.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** no express carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature," which implicitly captures fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** Insert an express carve-out overriding cl. 9.3, 12.8, 12.3/13 and 20.5. This is non-waivable under our playbook, and "any nature" language is the classic silent removal of fraud protection.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** general disclosure of the entire data room (as at 5pm 22 Sept 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** specific fair disclosure only.
- **Recommendation:** Delete DL 1.1–1.2 and limit disclosure to matters fairly and specifically disclosed against identified warranties. Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure guts the warranties.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** no claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl. 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** the blanket exclusion deleted. Any qualifier should apply to Seller knowledge only, limited to named persons after reasonable enquiry, and never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl. 8.3. It combines a blanket buyer-knowledge bar with constructive "discoverable" knowledge, which would neutralise the specific indemnities we are seeking for known issues (Ironquay, DD-006).

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** reasonable endeavours, with the condition deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent. DL 2 confirms that no final consent and no evidence of satisfaction of the cl. 11.3 conditions have been provided.
- **Buyer wants:** effective consent plus evidence that the cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a Completion condition.
- **Recommendation:** Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable-endeavours-only. Make effective consent with evidence of satisfied conditions a condition precedent, because Bluefen is roughly AUD 3.6m and about 30% of FY26 revenue.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** release "to be provided following Completion." DL 3 confirms the facility (~AUD 3.2m) is not repaid and no discharge has been provided.
- **Buyer wants:** a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject a post-Completion release. It would let us complete into encumbered shares and assets. Any post-Completion fallback needs an irrevocable bank undertaking plus Amelia Frost's approval, and neither exists.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** the DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs shown as a specific funds-flow line item (deducted or Debt-like) or demonstrably Seller-funded.
- **Recommendation:** Require an express funds-flow line item covering the bonuses and all on-costs, backed by an indemnity. The bonuses are triggered by Completion and would otherwise land on the Company, and therefore on us.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment, which the Seller considers adequate.
- **Buyer wants:** a broadened indemnity covering ownership, transfer and infringement risk for SOW3 Project Materials, while preserving the SOW3 cure mechanism (payment plus confirmatory assignment).
- **Recommendation:** Broaden the indemnity and require evidence of payment and a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable. The AUD 180,000 figure (DD-010) is not independently verified as either paid or unpaid, so the Seller should not anchor the indemnity to it, and we should not assume it either way.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** a "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **Buyer wants:** log preservation, a proper investigation, ongoing updates, and appropriate protection.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the materiality characterisation and impose interim covenants (preserve logs, investigate, provide updates and access) plus a specific indemnity. Nothing yet confirms or excludes a breach, harm or a notification duty, and we should assert no numeric loss in either direction.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** three renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** an assessment of timing, scope, terminability, accrual and whether the renewals are related-party, read together (DD-008/DD-011).
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label yet, and raise targeted DD requests. Equally, do not automatically treat the renewals as Debt or a price deduction, because the facts are undetermined (DL 8 is silent).

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** the cl. 12.3/13 "applies to all Claims" default and the "any nature" limitations collapse Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** separate categories, each with its own cap, time limit and threshold rules, and no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Rewrite the limitations so each applies only to General Warranty Claims unless expressly extended. This removes the override that drives N-004, N-005 and N-016.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register. DL 10 concedes this is the source relied on, not completed verification.
- **Buyer wants:** independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority.
- **Recommendation:** Treat DD-012 as an internal Seller source only. Require independent evidence (ASIC extract, PPSR search, board and shareholder approvals, constitutional review, and confirmation of no encumbrances, tied to the Riverlark release) plus a full Title warranty under the N-004 regime.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** these terms to remain OPEN. Unlimited liability should not be assumed, and the terms are not resolved.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "settled" characterisation and keep Tax and IP as open, separately negotiated categories. There has been no agreement, and folding them into a 20%/18-month regime would be a concession by default.

---

## Summary for the deal team
- **Nothing is agreed.** The [STANDARD] labels are unilateral and should be expressly rejected.
- **The draft at 20% / 18 months requires authority we do not have.** Do not concede either point without Amelia Frost's written approval identifying this draft.
- **Non-negotiables:** the fraud carve-out (N-005), a separate Title regime (N-004), and category separation (N-014).
- **Completion-critical items:** Bluefen consent with satisfied conditions (N-008), Riverlark payout and release at Completion (N-009), and the bonus line item (N-010).
- **Avoid overstatement in our mark-up:** do not assert that the Ironquay AUD 180,000 is unpaid, that DD-006 is a confirmed breach, or that the Sandbar renewals are Debt.
